title: Reports: PlayStation Network outages spike during 'Grand Theft Auto VI' release

 Reports: PlayStation Network outages spike during 'Grand Theft Auto VI' release
 Thousands of PlayStation users have experienced connection outages on the eve of one of the most anticipated video games in over a decade being released, according to multiple reports.

 By Joseph Ochoa, WRAL multiplatform producer, and wire reports
 Thousands of PlayStation users experienced connection outages during the release of Grand Theft Auto VI, one of the most anticipated video games in over a decade, according to multiple reports.
 Axios was the first to report news of the outage.
 Other WRAL Top Stories
 According to DownDetector , which tracks network outages across various platforms and services, more than 9,000 people were experiencing difficulty accessing PlayStation Network, an online service for PlayStation users, right at midnight when the game released. 
 As of 3:50 a.m. Thursday, outage reports had dropped to just over 100.
 PlayStation's status website , which tracks issues affecting issues with the console and PlayStation Network services, was reporting services are "up and running" as of 4 a.m.
 WRAL News has reached out to PlayStation about the reported outage and what may have caused it.
 The outages first began hours ahead of the release of Grand Theft Auto VI , which had been in production for years and is considered one of the most anticipated games of all time. Miami, which inspired the game's fictional location of "Vice City," is  paying homage to the new game .
 The “Grand Theft Auto” franchise has sold more than 470 million units worldwide. “Grand Theft Auto V,” released in 2013, accounts for more than 230 million of those sales and reached $1 billion in retail sales over just three days.
 The latest installment becomes playable at midnight local time on PlayStation 5 and Xbox consoles, meaning players in Asia and other regions will begin entering the game hours before its U.S. release. However, PlayStation announced on X that Sony Interactive, which owns PlayStation, issued a PlayStation 5 system update that the company says is required to play the game.
 New Zealand was among the first countries where players could access the game, and internet providers there were preparing for a surge in downloads as midnight arrived.
 “The game file size at 212 gigabytes is unprecedented,” said Kurt Rodgers, network strategy manager for Chorus New Zealand. “That’s more than a quarter of the average household’s data usage in an entire month, all in one go.”
 The company expects about 35 petabytes, or 35 million gigabytes, of additional traffic across its network, which Rodgers called “enormous.”
 The game has also received rave reviews and critical acclaim ahead of its release, receiving eight nominations from the Game Awards , including Game of the Year, and a Metacritic score of 99 out of 100, which the company rates as "universal acclaim."
 Grand Theft Auto VI is rated M (17+) by the ESRB for intense violence, blood and gore, sexual content, strong language, mature humor, and the use of drugs and alcohol.  
 The Associated Press contributed to this report .
